title: Film History and Cinema
text: Cinema was invented in the 1890s, with the Lumière brothers screening the first films publicly in Paris on December 28, 1895. Early films were silent and accompanied by live music. The first feature film is generally considered to be The Story of the Kelly Gang (1906). Sound films (talkies) began with The Jazz Singer (1927). Hollywood became the world's film production capital, establishing a studio system in the 1920s–1940s. The French New Wave (1950s–60s), Italian neorealism, and German Expressionism were significant artistic movements. The Academy Awards, first held in 1929, remain the most prestigious film honors. Digital filmmaking transformed production and distribution in the late 1990s–2000s.
